privacy.title: What is checked, and what is not
privacy.intro: Yasakia is for real people. When you add photos, Orazaka — Krizaka’s own AI platform, not a third-party service — looks at them once.

items.faces: Faces: it counts the faces in each photo and which one is the subject.
items.same: The same person — only if you agree: it can compare your face photos with each other, only to catch a photo that is clearly someone else. The comparison lasts a few seconds in memory; no face print is kept, anywhere.
items.questions: Three yes/no questions to a vision model: does it look like a screenshot, is something written over it (text, a number, a username), does the person look under 18?
items.not: Not checked: who you are. It identifies no one and recognises no celebrity.

privacy.limits: It can be wrong, especially with a lookalike, a hat, strong light or a small face. If a photo is refused and you think it should not be, choose another one of you.

comparison.OFF: Your photos are not compared with each other: faces are only counted.
comparison.NEEDS_CONSENT: Your photos are not compared with each other until you agree above: faces are only counted.
comparison.ON: With your agreement, your photos are compared with each other to catch a photo of someone else. Nothing is kept.

consent.title: Compare my photos with each other?
consent.lead: To make sure your face photos show the same person, we can compare them with each other. This is facial analysis, so we ask you first.
consent.purpose: We compare your photos with each other to check they show the same person. Nothing is kept: the comparison lasts a few seconds in memory, and no face print is stored anywhere.
consent.nothingKept: Only the result is kept — a note such as « face detected » — never a face print, a score or a copy of the comparison.
consent.optional: You can say no, or take your agreement back at any time. Without it, we only count the faces in your photos and look for text and screenshots.

intros.title: Introductions
intros.lead: Two people said yes to each other: a private room for seven days. Continue together, or let it fade.
intros.emptyDescription: When someone you said yes to says yes too, your introduction opens here.
intros.frozen: Paused while a report is reviewed.
intros.agentNeverReads: Your agent never reads this conversation. To show the small mark above each message, a classifier reads each message once, on Krizaka’s own servers, and keeps nothing; the mark is a signal that can be wrong, never a verdict.
intros.continueLead: Want to keep talking after the seven days? It continues when you both say so.
intros.waitingForThem: You said you want to continue. Waiting for {name}.
intros.typedByYou: Every message here is typed by you two. The agent writes nothing for you and never reads this conversation.

HAND.label: Written by hand
HAND.hint: Nothing points to this message being generated: it was typed here, at a human pace.

UNSURE.label: Uncertain
UNSURE.hint: We cannot tell. A signal is not a verdict: many people paste a message they wrote elsewhere.

LIKELY_GENERATED.label: Probably generated
LIKELY_GENERATED.hint: The text reads like machine text and it arrived pasted or faster than a hand types. It may be a message the person wrote elsewhere.

TOO_SHORT.label: Too short to judge
TOO_SHORT.hint: A short text says too little to say anything.

authenticity.canBeWrong: This signal can be wrong, especially on short texts and on French or non-native writing. It never blocks a message.
